interpretation: Free recovery spontaneously develops substantial row-plus-input-group scale structure, matching the qualitative public-checkpoint finding.

A mild binary residual penalty at coefficient 0.1 improves teacher KL in five of six paired runs and lowers the pooled mean by 1.32%, but six pairs are insufficient for a high-confidence mandatory-default claim.
Ternary coefficients show no stable behavior advantage in this sample; the nominal coefficient-1 winner improves only three of six pairs.

Very strong penalties can drive scale additive R2 above 0.999 while changing teacher KL only modestly, showing that most free per-group scale residuals are not essential on the miniature. Public checkpoints nevertheless retain measurable residual structure, so a soft prior is more faithful than a hard separability constraint.
Current implementation decision: retain free per-group scales; expose an optional mild row/group residual regularizer; run a larger paired confirmation before making it a release-matched default.
